Title: Changing the narrative in Educational Leadership
NewsSummary: IED, EA launches a diploma programme in Education Leadership and Management
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan Universitys' Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (AKU-IED, EA) has launched a two-year diploma programme in Education Leadership and Management. The diploma, under the Foundations for Learning (F4L) project, is targeted at school leaders, head teachers and their deputies. AKU-IED, EA is partnering with the Kenya Education Management Institute (KEMI) to deliver the curriculum. 

To kick it off, a six-day workshop was held in the coastal county of Mombasa with participation from 26 school administrators. Some of the programme's foccus areas include: Leadership strategy development and decision making; administration and crisis management as well as action research skills.

"The training has set the bar on significance of capacity building to drive improvement and efficiency in our work. This is all about change management, mind mapping and understanding the context of issues and challenges that arise in work environments. Change usually comes from within the school leader and trickles down to the teachers, learners, and stakeholders hence the saying, we lead by example," said Grace Gatundu, National Management Trainer at KEMI.

In 2017, Kenya rolled out a new education system, the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC) to replace the old system. The diploma programme is expected to enhance the capacity of teachers and school administrators to effectively implement the curriculum. 

''I have heard about portfolio generally as an assessment rubric for Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC) learners. I didn't know that there is a professional learning portfolio that can be made by teachers and school leaders. It is important to develop a portfolio since it depicts the efforts, progress and achievements made by a leader to show that work is going on in an institution,'' said Alice Okonye from Ziwa la Ng'ombe Primary School.

AKU-IED, EA will continue to support the education systems across East Africa to make champion leaders who can be critical thinkers and problem solvers as they transform to be change agents in their communities and their countries.

"I am happy to be part of the transformation journey of these school leaders who are the drivers of change in their workplace. The school leaders will also acquire research skills in particular action research, this will enable them to identify a problem and assess the cause of the problem and come up with an action to solve this problem," acknowledged Philemon Righa, Professional Development Tutor and Trainer at AKU-IED, EA

 F4L will continue to build capacity of head of schools leadership styles and approaches focusing greatly on gender responsiveness and inclusivity facets.
